title: Isolated site deployment verification and upgrade safety criteria
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Define a clear set of functional requirements and acceptance criteria for deploying Redwood Private into isolated customer networks (no-egress / restricted egress) and for performing in-place upgrades with guaranteed rollback and minimal application disruption. This ticket captures validation checks, required telemetry, operator runbooks, and non-functional constraints (timing windows, bandwidth, signing). It also resolves ambiguous scope from earlier PRDs around 'offline upgrades' by providing explicit artifact sync and verification steps.
scope_in: Acceptance criteria for first-time install into isolated VPCs with one-way egress-proxy
Upgrade validation plan for minor and patch image updates in air-gapped environments
Artifact signing and checksum verification steps for offline image sync
Network-level probes and health checks that run without outbound DNS/HTTP access
Operator rollback criteria and automated state capture for post-mortem
scope_out: Building a new remote artifact distribution product (we will consume existing customer sync pipelines)
Full CI pipeline changes for customer images
Platform-managed certificate issuance inside customer networks
acceptance_criteria: Install: Given a customer VPC with no direct external egress, the installer completes if all artifacts are present on a local mirror and checksums/signatures match; installer exits non-zero with a human-readable error if validation fails.

Network verification: The platform exposes a 'network-status' report that lists required ports/protocols and verifies local DNS resolution against a provided internal resolver; the check must pass without contacting public endpoints.

Upgrade dry-run: For any image update, a dry-run mode must validate compatibility of runtime config, kernel/driver constraints, and available disk space. Dry-run must complete within the configured maintenance window or abort with an explicit reason.

Rollback: If post-upgrade health checks (startup probes, KV cache warmup, and per-node latency SLOs) fail within the configured grace period, the system must automatically trigger a rollback to the last-known-good image and record a traceable event with artifacts attached.

Auditability: Every install/upgrade/rollback must create an immutable audit entry (timestamp, operator id, artifacts checksums, pre/post health snapshots) that can be exported via the Private admin console or an S3-compatible bucket behind the customer's network.

Bandwidth/timeout tolerances: Offline artifact sync must support intermittent connections; installer retries must be configurable, and the installer should support resumable downloads and a configurable global timeout.
Operator runbook: There must be a single-step runbook (markdown) under the customer's support bundle that explains validation, manual rollback, and emergency escape actions.
Security: All artifacts used in isolated installs or upgrades must be signed; the installer must reject unsigned or tampered artifacts and provide the signature chain for inspection.
non_functional_requirements: Installer must complete within a configurable maintenance window (default 60 minutes) for small clusters (<8 GPUs);
Log verbosity for install/upgrade path must include at least INFO for success paths and DEBUG for failures and be exportable over syslog or local file collection;
Upgrade processes must not increase 99th percentile request latency by more than 25% for more than 2 minutes during canary phases;
comments: 2025-02-14: Initial scoping review with SRE and Security. Security asked for artifact signing by default; added as AC.
2025-02-20: Engineering raised concern about resumable downloads for large model artifacts; added bandwidth/timeout non-functional requirements.
2025-02-27: UX asked for a compact 'network-status' export format to attach to support bundles; added requirement.
2025-03-03: PM sync: moved from Triage to Planned pending ENG-4092 rework; security review flagged as required.
implementation_notes: Prefer using existing internal artifact verifier library (eng/pkg/artifact-verifier) to validate signatures and checksums.
Dry-run should reuse the canary orchestration path used by Dedicated autoscale to simulate traffic and validate latency impacts.
Audit entries must be serializable as JSONL and stored on the customer mirror or exported to their S3-compatible endpoint.
risks: Customers may have heterogeneous internal mirrors with inconsistent checksum behavior; mitigation: provide a lightweight mirror-validator tool.
Air-gapped upgrades can be slow for large models; mitigation: support incremental/resumable sync and recommend pre-staging artifacts outside maintenance windows.
